name: Create a section under a class, assign its class incharge, and hold its parent WhatsApp group link
priorityReason: Students are placed into sections, not classes. Nothing can be placed until sections exist.

goal.capability: to create the sections under a class, assign the class incharge and subjects, and hold the section's parent group link
goal.outcome: students can be placed, and their guardians reach the right parent group without anyone hunting for a link

secondaryActors.involvement: Creates sections, and creates the section's WhatsApp group in WhatsApp and records its invite link here.
Approves the section structure, oversees the groups, and may create sections themselves.
Sees only the sections assigned to them.
Is sent the section's invite link when their child is placed in it.

externalActors.involvement: Holds the actual parent group. The group is created there by hand, and only its invite link is stored here (BR-4).

additional.description: A class is created and sections are then created under it.

preconditions.condition: The class exists for the academic session.
An authenticated session exists and the acting user is Coordinator, Staff or School Admin.
The staff member being assigned as class incharge exists and is active.
For the group link, the WhatsApp group has already been created by hand in WhatsApp and its invite link copied (BR-4).

postConditions: The section exists under its class, with a class incharge and its subjects assigned.
Students can now be placed into it, which is the point of creating it.
The section's WhatsApp invite link is stored against it, so a guardian is sent the right link automatically when their child is placed.
The class incharge sees the section in their own list and can mark its attendance.
A change to the section, its incharge or its group link appears everywhere the section is used.
Where the link was replaced, the new link is the one used for every placement from then on, and guardians already placed are not re-invited automatically.
No student is placed by creating a section, and no WhatsApp group is created by the system.

dataFields.name: Class

dataFields.name: Section name
dataFields.validation: 1 to 30 characters. Unique within the class (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Capacity
dataFields.validation: 1 to 200. The number of students the section holds, which placement and admission both check against (BR-6).

dataFields.name: Class incharge
dataFields.validation: The teacher responsible for the section. Required, because attendance and day-to-day matters have to belong to somebody (BR-5).

dataFields.name: Subjects
dataFields.validation: The subjects this section carries, drawn from the class's subjects. A section cannot carry a subject the class does not (BR-7).

dataFields.name: WhatsApp group invite link
dataFields.validation: The invite link of the group created by hand in WhatsApp. Stored, not generated. Must be a WhatsApp invite address (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Group link recorded on
dataFields.validation: When the link was stored or last replaced.

dataFields.name: Placed count
dataFields.validation: How many students are currently placed, shown against the capacity.

businessRules.rule: Students are placed into sections, not into classes. A class with no sections holds nobody.
A section belongs to one class and cannot be moved to another. Moving it would take its students with it.
A section name is unique within its class. Two Section Bs under Grade 4 make every register ambiguous.

The WhatsApp group is created by hand in WhatsApp and only its invite link is stored here. A group created through the WhatsApp Business API is capped at eight participants, which is fewer than a section holds, so the system stores a link rather than managing a group.
A section has a class incharge from the moment it is created. Attendance and day-to-day matters have to belong to somebody.
A section has a capacity, and placement and admission both check against it. A section is never over-filled by either route.
A section carries only subjects its class carries. A Fixed class's sections carry all of them; a Subject Wise class's sections may carry a subset.
Storing the invite link is what makes placement automatic. When a student is placed, the guardian is sent the link held against that section, without anyone looking it up.

A replaced link is the one used for every placement from then on. Guardians already placed are not re-invited automatically, because a group has not necessarily changed just because its link was regenerated.
A section without a stored link can still take students. Placement records that no link was sent, so the gap is visible rather than silent.
A change to a section, its incharge or its group link is reflected everywhere the section is used.
A section is deactivated, never deleted, and cannot be deactivated while a student is still placed in it.

transitions.condition: The placed count reaches the capacity (BR-6).
A student is moved out, or the capacity is raised.
No student remains placed in it (BR-12).
The section is reinstated within the same session.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Class & Session → Class detail → Create section
basicFlow.userAction: Opens a class and starts a section under it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Loads the form scoped to that class and its subjects.

basicFlow.userAction: Enters the section name and its capacity.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the name is unique within the class.

basicFlow.navigation: Create section → Class incharge and subjects
basicFlow.userAction: Assigns the class incharge and the subjects the section carries.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Requires a class incharge, and refuses any subject the class does not carry.

basicFlow.navigation: Creates the group in WhatsApp, outside the system
basicFlow.userAction: Creates the section's parent group in WhatsApp and copies its invite link.
Pastes the invite link into the section record.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Validates it is a WhatsApp invite address and stores it against the section with who recorded it and when.
Creates the section, which students can now be placed into.
Makes the section readable by attendance, timetable and the class incharge's own lists.

alternateFlows.condition: The group has not been created in WhatsApp yet
alternateFlows.behaviour: The section is saved without a link and can still take students. Each placement records that no link was sent, so the gap is visible rather than silent (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The group link is replaced later
alternateFlows.behaviour: The new link is used for every placement from then on. Guardians already placed are not re-invited automatically, and the previous link stays in the history (BR-9).
The new incharge sees the section in their list and the previous one no longer does. The change is reflected in attendance and timetable at once (BR-11).
The section carries a subset of the class's subjects rather than all of them, which is what timetable and results read afterwards (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: A section is no longer run
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is deactivated only once no student remains placed in it. It stays readable in historical reports (BR-12).

alternateFlows.condition: A guardian already placed needs the link again
alternateFlows.behaviour: The stored link is sent again to that guardian and the send is logged, without re-inviting the whole section.

openQuestions.question: Should replacing a group link re-invite the guardians already placed?
openQuestions.assumption: No (BR-9). A resend control exists for doing it deliberately.

openQuestions.question: Who is responsible for creating the WhatsApp group — Staff or the class incharge?
openQuestions.assumption: Staff, per the feature. Not confirmed.

openQuestions.question: Should a section be blocked from taking students until a group link is stored?
openQuestions.assumption: No. The gap is recorded instead (BR-10).

openQuestions.question: Is the class incharge the same person as the section's main subject teacher?
openQuestions.assumption: Not necessarily. Subject teachers are assigned through the timetable.

openQuestions.question: What happens to a stored link when the group is deleted in WhatsApp?
openQuestions.assumption: The system cannot know. It fails when a guardian taps it. Not specified.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
